details.description: DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B is an 8-billion-parameter reasoning model that DeepSeek created by distilling chain-of-thought traces from its updated DeepSeek-R1-0528 model onto a Qwen3-8B Base checkpoint. Fireworks AI serves it as deepseek-r1-0528-distill-qwen3-8b with a 131,000-token context window. DeepSeek's own model card reports the distilled model surpasses the plain Qwen3-8B model by 10 percentage points on AIME 2024 and matches the much larger Qwen3-235B-thinking model on that same benchmark. It is released under the MIT license.
advantages: Scores 86.0% pass@1 on AIME 2024, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
Scores 76.3% pass@1 on AIME 2025, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
Scores 61.1% on GPQA Diamond, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
DeepSeek reports the model surpasses the base Qwen3-8B model by 10 percentage points on AIME 2024 and matches the far larger Qwen3-235B-thinking model on that benchmark.
disadvantages: 8-billion-parameter model; DeepSeek's model card compares it only to Qwen3 models, not to the full DeepSeek-R1-0528 it was distilled from.
DeepSeek's model card and usage templates cover only Chinese and English, with no other languages stated.

DeepSeek's own API changelog labels this reasoning generation 'legacy R1' and discontinued the deepseek-reasoner model id in favor of the DeepSeek-V4 series by July 2026, though the open weights stay available on Hugging Face and via third-party hosts such as Fireworks AI.
use_cases: General question-answering with an explicit chain-of-thought reasoning step

notes: DeepSeek's own repo name for this checkpoint omits 'Distill' (DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B), but its model card confirms it is the same model as Fireworks' deepseek-r1-0528-distill-qwen3-8b: chain-of-thought distilled from DeepSeek-R1-0528 onto a Qwen3-8B Base. DeepSeek's model card does not state an explicit context-length figure; Fireworks' listing states 131k tokens, matching the catalog's 131,072 max_input/max_output facts, which are kept as-is. The model card itself points to the deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1 GitHub repo ('for more information about running DeepSeek-R1-0528 locally'), so github_url is set to that repo even though its own model table does not list this specific checkpoint. DeepSeek's own API changelog (api-docs.deepseek.com/updates) shows deepseek-reasoner moved from DeepSeek-R1-0528 to DeepSeek-V3.1/V3.2-Exp in 2025 and then to the discontinued-legacy V4 transition by mid-2026, referring to this generation as 'legacy R1'.
